findings.description: The reports_archive bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the vendor roster seeded into it) are stored with only S3's baseline; there is no enforced KMS/SSE configuration, so sensitive report data is not protected at rest under a managed key and could be exposed if the bucket is accessed or compromised.

reports_archive defines no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block nor any policy to deny public access, and it is named for sensitive reports; without block_public_acls/block_public_policy/restrict_public_buckets, any later ACL or policy change can expose the bucket publicly.
Versioning is not enabled on reports_archive, so overwritten or deleted objects (e.g., the vendor roster) cannot be recovered and tampering/ransomware deletion is not mitigated.
No logging block targets the audit_trail bucket, so access to reports_archive is not recorded and unauthorized reads cannot be detected or investigated.
ledger_exports has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so financial ledger exports are stored without enforced encryption-at-rest under an explicit SSE/KMS configuration.
ledger_exports sets acl = "private" but provides no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block and no deny-public policy, so the private setting can be overridden and the sensitive ledger data exposed.
Versioning is not enabled on ledger_exports, so deletions or overwrites of financial ledger exports are unrecoverable and cannot be audited.
No logging block is configured for ledger_exports, leaving access to sensitive ledger exports unaudited.
model_artifacts has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so model artifacts are stored without enforced encryption at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing tags and public access block
findings.description: model_artifacts has an empty tags block and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so there is no governance metadata and no layer preventing the bucket from being made public.
ops_runbooks has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so operational runbooks (which often contain sensitive procedures, hostnames, and credentials) are unencrypted at rest.
ops_runbooks relies only on acl = "private" with no public access block or bucket policy denying public access, so the runbooks could be exposed by a later ACL or policy change.
ops_runbooks has versioning but no logging block, so access to runbooks is not recorded to the audit trail.

audit_trail uses acl = "log-delivery-write" and defines no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block nor a policy restricting access to the log-delivery service principal, so the audit trail may be readable or writable beyond intended consumers, undermining its integrity.

reports_seed_object uploads vendor-roster.xlsx (a vendor PII/commercial data file) into reports_archive, which has no default encryption configured, so the sensitive object is written without explicit SSE/KMS encryption at rest.
